clue.text: How top golfer can play without practising?

definitions.text: How top golfer can play without practising?

parts.words: How top golfer can play without practising?
parts.note: a golfer with no handicap is a 'scratch' player, and a phrase meaning starting with no preparation at all fits the second half

explanation.surface: A question about how the best golfers manage to play well without any practice.
explanation.walkthrough: A scratch golfer plays off a handicap of zero, so a top golfer plays off scratch; the phrase also means beginning with nothing done in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means starting from nothing, with no preparation, which is what playing without practising implies.

clue.text: Audible sign of relief it's not a 7ac

indicators.note: audible means heard, so the word for the sign of relief is said aloud

parts.note: phew is the exclamation of relief

explanation.surface: Someone sighs with relief that something isn't a big deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 across is LOT, so 'not a 7ac' is 'not a lot'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small number of things is not many, the opposite of a large quantity.

clue.text: Basket-maker more comfortable when head cold is gone

indicators.note: the head letter has departed, so it is taken out of the word for more comfortable

parts.note: cosier means snugger, more comfortable

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A basket-weaver feels better once a head cold has cleared up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head cold' looks like the illness, but 'head' picks C, the first letter of 'cold', which leaves COSIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Willow shoots of this kind are cut and woven into baskets, so the plant provides basketry material.

clue.text: Check what one losing in court wants?

definitions.meaning: a hold-up or reverse in progress

definitions.text: what one losing in court wants?
definitions.meaning: a tennis player losing a match on court would like to win back a set

explanation.surface: A litigant who is losing a case wants to put a stop to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a law court, but it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverse or hindrance to progress is a check; a tennis player wants to get a set back.

clue.text: Cause riot, having set up one to go into prison

parts.note: to raise is to set up or erect

indicators.note: the one goes inside the prison word, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: can is slang for prison
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A prison riot is started after someone frames a person to be jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make a great disturbance or fuss, as rioters do.

clue.text: Doctor's entertainment

definitions.meaning: to give medical care to someone
a special pleasure or outing paid for by someone else

explanation.surface: A physician's idea of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a patient medical care is the verb sense; a pleasure provided for someone is the noun sense.

clue.text: Throwing the game

definitions.meaning: flinging with force
an Irish stick-and-ball field sport

explanation.surface: Losing on purpose, throwing a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throwing the game' reads as deliberately losing, but it is two definitions; HURLING is an Irish field sport.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurl is to fling; hurling is also the traditional Irish sport played with sticks.

clue.text: Execution for conspiracy is one's fate

indicators.note: executing the conspiracy word by beheading it means its first letter is cut off

parts.note: a conspiracy is a plot

explanation.surface: A conspirator learns that being executed for the plot is his destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Execution' here means beheading: PLOT loses its head, the P.
explanation.definitionFit: Your lot in life is your destiny or fortune.

clue.text: To function as parliament, stage one is to get some candidates

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
I is the Roman numeral for one
a slate is a list of candidates for election

explanation.surface: To act as a parliament, the first stage is to find some candidates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is to get' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Making laws is the core function of a parliament.

clue.text: Enthusiastic expression, following inviting pairs of hips

definitions.meaning: a rousing shout of approval
the call 'hip, hip' is answered each time by 'hooray'

explanation.surface: A keen remark that follows an invitation, seemingly about hips.
explanation.walkthrough: The leader's 'Hip, hip!' (a pair of hips) invites each 'Hooray!', given three times over.
explanation.definitionFit: A triple shout of hooray is a traditional show of enthusiasm.

clue.text: It was wrong to cover inside centre circle

indicators.note: the words 'It was' are put wrong, rearranged into a new order

parts.note: to line something is to cover its inside surface

explanation.surface: Someone complains it was a mistake to put a covering inside the centre circle of a football pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges IT WAS to WAIST. 'Centre circle' looks like the football pitch marking, but it means the ring round the body's middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The line round a person's middle is a circle drawn round the body's centre.

clue.text: I've got it! It's a boy

definitions.meaning: radio operators say this word to confirm a message has been received and understood
it is also a boy's first name

explanation.surface: A new parent's excited announcement on hearing that the baby is a son.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio talk the word acknowledges a message, and it is also a common male first name.

clue.text: Painter secured by boat that blocks river

indicators.note: the painter is held fast inside the boat word, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a barge is a flat-bottomed river boat
RA stands for Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A boat's painter, its mooring rope, is tied to a vessel that is blocking the river.
explanation.walkthrough: A painter is also the rope that ties up a boat, which makes the surface nautical; in crosswords a painter is often RA, Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: A dam or weir built across a river to hold back water is called by this name.

clue.text: Type who was dogged by misfortune?

definitions.meaning: a classic serif typeface named after an 18th-century Birmingham printer
the family in a Sherlock Holmes story haunted by a hound

explanation.surface: A person who has been plagued by bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dogged' is literal: in The Hound of the Baskervilles the family is pursued by a spectral dog.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a classic serif typeface, and the name of the Conan Doyle family cursed by a hound.

clue.text: Second piece of lemon put into miserable port

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, the letter going into the word for miserable

parts.note: triste is an old word, from French, for sad or miserable

indicators.note: the second letter of the following word is the piece used

explanation.surface: A slice of lemon dropped into a glass of bad port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink in the surface but is the definition, a harbour town; TRIESTE is a port in north-east Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is an Italian seaport on the Adriatic, so it is an example of a harbour city.

clue.text: Baffled, being pointedly held up

definitions.meaning: unable to solve something, at a loss
pinned on something sharp, as an insect is fixed on a pin

explanation.surface: Someone is puzzled at being held up so sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at a loss is being stumped, and something impaled on a pin has been fixed there.

clue.text: In revolt, children asked originally to wear school caps

parts.note: people up in arms are in revolt

indicators.note: the initials are dressed in the school word, so they sit inside it

parts.note: the Perse is a school in Cambridge

indicators.note: originally means taking the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: Rebellious pupils are asked to put on their school caps.
explanation.walkthrough: THE PERSE is an independent school in Cambridge, England. 'caps' looks like headgear but means capital letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters are often shortened to caps, and printers call them by this name.

clue.text: Star name hooked

parts.note: a fan who manages to get a celebrity's signature has 'hooked' that star's name

explanation.surface: Read as a fishing triumph: a famous name has been caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity's signature collected by a fan is the star's name captured on paper.

clue.text: International contest finally won by gifted horse

definitions.meaning: a war between nations
the Greeks ended the siege of Troy using a wooden horse given as a gift

explanation.surface: A sporting event decided at the end by a talented horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gifted' looks like talented but means given as a gift: the wooden horse left for the Trojans.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary conflict between Greeks and Trojans ended through the wooden horse trick.

clue.text: No repeats broadcast? Nobody understands it, naturally

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered about, so the letters of the fodder are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint about programmes being repeated, and a language nobody grasps.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a joke: the invented language has almost no native speakers, so nobody understands it naturally, from birth.
explanation.definitionFit: The artificial international language was constructed, so almost no one speaks it as a mother tongue.

clue.text: Football team's fury, having extremely ridiculous clothing

indicators.note: the outer letters dress the other piece, so it goes inside them
extremely means taking the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: anger is fury

explanation.surface: A football team is furious at being made to wear absurd kit.
explanation.walkthrough: RANGERS is a Glasgow football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangers is a Scottish football club based in Glasgow.

clue.text: Cheshire town where people have made a lot of changes

definitions.meaning: a town in Cheshire, a county in north-west England

definitions.text: where people have made a lot of changes
definitions.meaning: a famous railway junction where passengers change trains

explanation.surface: A northern English town that has been heavily redeveloped.
explanation.walkthrough: CREWE is a railway town and junction where many travellers change trains, which is the second sense of 'changes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewe is a town in Cheshire famous as a rail junction for switching between trains.

clue.text: Makes a move in game that's nil-nil, it appears

definitions.text: Makes a move in game that's nil-nil, it appears

parts.words: Makes a move in game that's nil-nil, it appears
parts.note: a chess move whose written notation looks like a goalless score, 0-0

explanation.surface: A player makes a move in a match that is still goalless.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess notation, castling on the king's side is written O-O, which looks like nil-nil.
explanation.definitionFit: Castling, moving king and rook together, is recorded as O-O, resembling a nil-nil score.

clue.text: Queen welcomed by museum gallery

indicators.note: the queen is taken in by the museum, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen is received at a museum's gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A (the Victoria and Albert Museum in London) is spelt out V AND A.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery can be a covered porch or balcony along the outside of a building.

clue.text: Bikini, perhaps, about to show everything

definitions.text: Bikini, perhaps, about to show everything

parts.words: Bikini, perhaps, about to show everything
parts.note: Bikini is also a ring of coral islands in the Pacific, and the swimsuit reading is the joke

explanation.surface: A skimpy swimsuit on the verge of revealing all.
explanation.walkthrough: Bikini is a Pacific coral island group, used for nuclear tests, after which the swimsuit was named.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini in the Marshall Islands is a ring-shaped coral reef enclosing a lagoon.

clue.text: Trials using old weight and measures

parts.note: the as was an ancient Roman unit of weight
sizes are measurements

explanation.surface: Tests carried out with old-fashioned weights and measures.
explanation.walkthrough: ASSIZES were the periodic criminal courts held in English counties until 1972.
explanation.definitionFit: The assizes were sessions of court for hearing cases, so the word names judicial hearings.

clue.text: Unknown river in African country

parts.note: z is a letter used for an unknown quantity in algebra
the Aire is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: An unidentified river somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aire is a river in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Zaire was the name of the Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1971 to 1997.

clue.text: Permission for elder, say, to respond to promptings of spring

definitions.meaning: authorisation, as in ... to go

definitions.text: for elder, say, to respond to promptings of spring
definitions.meaning: an elder is a tree, and trees put out foliage in spring

explanation.surface: An older person seeks permission to answer the urges of springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elder' looks like an older person but is the tree; to leave is to come into leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Being granted leave is being allowed; a tree that comes into leaf is said to leave.

clue.text: Like some novels from author Well I analysed some

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone has studied a few books by a writer called Well.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiction like Nineteen Eighty-Four, by George Orwell, depicts totalitarian control and is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Raise money that might make you an egghead, so to speak?

definitions.text: that might make you an egghead, so to speak?
definitions.note: a louse egg in the hair could jokingly give you an egg head

indicators.note: raising a word in a down clue lifts it upwards, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: Raising cash that could turn you into an intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' means an intellectual, but here it is a head with eggs in it: a louse egg in the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A head louse's egg in the hair would make your head literally egg-laden.

clue.text: She makes time before 4 — that she did!

definitions.text: She makes time before 4 — that she did!

parts.words: She makes time before 4 — that she did!
parts.note: the woman's name is also a word for the time just before an event, and the first woman raised Cain, the clue at 4

explanation.surface: A woman sets aside time before four o'clock, and an exclamation that she certainly did.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 down is RAISE CAIN: in Genesis the first woman bore and raised Cain. Her name also means the day or evening before something.
explanation.definitionFit: The first woman in Genesis was mother of Cain, and her name means the period just before an occasion.

clue.text: Less perfect, erring in pride

indicators.note: going astray, so the letters of the two words wander into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Being less than perfect comes from making mistakes out of vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erring' rearranges LESS PERFECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper regard for one's own worth and dignity is a kind of pride.
